Sorry, but that’s unfortunately not true. You don’t learn to understand coding just by looking at it and analyzing it. You learn to code by coding yourself and encountering problems that only come up during the process, or by discovering mistakes you’ve made. You don’t learn to play the piano or compose music by analyzing music either, you only learn it by doing it. The danger is that people won’t even be able to change simple things in the code anymore because they no longer understand the context and won‘t be able to improvise. They are literally unarmed without AI. Use AI as a teacher or assistant, but not as your brain.

to help people understand AI i'll explain it quickly, google and wikipedia lets you search for information and links to information, and that was great but you could never actually read all that information, AI or a LLM (large language model) has already read all that information, so when you prompt it, it can tell about all the important things that following all the links and reading all the information might have given you, that's extremely powerful.. how it does it you probably already know, it's very simple, we give every word a precise number we can adjust, then a bunch of tables with some more numbers we can adjust, and as we train an AI or process a large amount of information, it uses all previous words (context) and their values combined to predict the next word, and if it's wrong it adjusts all the values so it's not wrong or less wrong, and what happens is that eventually after a lot of training, the tables of numbers become very very good at predicting the next logical word base on the words you give it (context) in the form of a question or request, and it can just keep predicting words.... HOWEVER... that's the simple part.. how it really works is that we use a program that adds stuff to our questions and requests (context)... hidden words that say don't explain how to make bad things and much more.. but the program also uses the model to expand the question you asked, and to predict what your real question or goals might be and then use it again to get you a better answer... and that's very powerful.. and we call that program the COMPOSER... and now we have programs called agents that can use AI automatically... and that can learn and try new things.. or just do repetitive tasks base on various inputs.. now it's also important to understand that it takes a lot of numbers and computation to make a LLM work.. we might use 1 to 10 GPUs (graphics gards) or AI specific chips, to make a big LLM work, basically there's some with 20 billion parameters/numbers and some with 200 billion parameters/numbers.. and that's why we need data centers because it's cheaper to share access to 10 GPUs than buy 10 each.. but also, we've now split models into a bunch of smaller models we call experts, so we don't have to load it all at once... but really the amazing thing is the composers.. they're able to search the internet and use information as context or data.. and the composer is able to use the LLM to write computer code or stories or summaries extremely fast.. right now i have a project in ChatGPT that basically is just about getting me news that i want on video games, tv, movies, stocks, and more... the LLM is just like the engine.. it wasn't trained on the new movies released today.. it's the composer that used the LLM to determine what to search for.. it may say the user said it likes resident evil so what should we search for.. and it do hundreds of questions like this... so what's really doing the work.. the composer or the LLM.. i think it's both.. a better LLM helps predict better but there's only so much knowledge and things you can predict... and only so much knowledge you can train it on... but the composer we can be improving for centuries.. it's like endless perhaps... so now that you understand it fully, you should be able to wield this great power... i had it write webpages for many websites.. custom mini apps to make a slideshow or batch manipulate files.. careful with that though.. i do have experience and i did catch many mistakes and i did have to give it the correct method often... but when i did it recognized it and did it.. it was a struggle at first.. many retests.. many asks to check code.. but so many things it solved as well.. also note that AI can generate images and use images as input or context.. it can really be useful as a quick prototype visual but it's pretty bad and good at the same time.. i know a video AI called seedance 2 is amazing i think but i wouldn't pay for it without a client for now.. i also have local AI with my 5070ti that's decent but it's not as good as big company AI.. the composer is not the same... it doesn't search the internet.. and with only 16GB vram i can only use small models with not as many parameters.. but it's free but so is google gemini and chatgpt to some degree.. haven't really used claude or grok.. that's about it, i was very behind the curve i think, i have caught up or at least i understand it well now, there's much more detail on the tables and how they work together in an LLM but it's not that important, the next step might be agents, but i don't have a use yet.. i think if you have a company to automate mail and support then it's pretty huge.. OH, I also just seen chatgpt astra 6 i think, that looks sick, like it can use blender and other apps for you, i was using chatgpt to help write unreal engine code but it might do it directly now, and really again that's the composer i think, it's super advanced, and when you understand that you can use it, realize what it can do best of luck.. work smarter not harder
